readings.subsection: The Increase of the Covenant Family
readings.title: Seventy Beings in Mitsrayim
readings.subtitle: The Biological Foundation of Yisra’ĕl
readings.text:
[Exodus 1:1] And these are the names of the children of Yisra’ĕl who came to Mitsrayim with <dn>את</dn> Ya‘aqoḇ, each one with his household:
[2] Re’uḇĕn, Shim‘on, Lĕvi, and Yehuḏah;
[3] Yissasḵar, Zeḇulun, and Binyamin;
[4] Dan and Naphtali, Gaḏ and Ashĕr.
[5] And all those who were descendants of Ya‘aqoḇ were seventy beings, as Yosĕph was already in Mitsrayim.
[6] And Yosĕph died, and all his brothers, and all that generation.
[7] And the children of Yisra’ĕl were fruitful and increased very much, multiplied and became very strong, and the land was filled with them.

readings.title: The Rise of the New Sovereign
readings.subtitle: The Systemic Affliction of the Hebrews
readings.text:
[8] Then a new sovereign arose over Mitsrayim, who did not know <dn>את</dn> Yosĕph,
[9] and he said to his people, “See, the people of the children of Yisra’ĕl are more and stronger than we,
[10] come, let us act wisely towards them, lest they increase, and it shall be when fighting befalls us, that they shall join our enemies and fight against us, and shall go up out of the land.”
[11] So they set slave-masters over them to afflict them with their burdens, and they built for Pharaoh supply cities, <dn>את</dn> Pithom and <dn>את</dn> Ra‘amses.
[12] But the more they afflicted them, the more they increased and grew, and they were in dread of the children of Yisra’ĕl.
[13] And the Mitsrites made <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ĕl serve with harshness,
[14] and they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in mortar, and in brick, and in all kinds of work in the field, <dn>את</dn> all their work which they made them do was with harshness.

readings.title: The Hebrew Midwives
readings.subtitle: Fearing Elohim Over the State
readings.text:
[15] Then the sovereign of Mitsrayim spoke to the Hebrew midwives, of whom the name of one was Shiphrah and the name of the other Pu‘ah,
[16] and he said, “When you deliver <dn>את</dn> the Hebrew women, and see them on the birthstools, if it is a son, then you shall put <dn>את</dn> him to death, but if it is a daughter, then she shall live.”
[17] But the midwives feared <dn>את</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, and did not do as the sovereign of Mitsrayim commanded them, and kept <dn>את</dn> the male children alive.
[18] So the sovereign of Mitsrayim called for the midwives and said to them, “Why have you done this, and kept <dn>את</dn> the male children alive?”
[19] And the midwives said to Pharaoh, “Because the Hebrew women are not like the Mitsrian women. For they are lively and give birth before the midwives come to them.”
[20] So <dn>Elohim</dn> was good to the midwives, and the people increased and became very numerous.
[21] And it came to be, because the midwives feared <dn>את</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, that <dn>He</dn> provided households for them.
[22] And Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, “Throw every son who is born into the river, and keep alive every daughter.”

readings.title: The Ark in the Reeds
readings.subtitle: Drawn from the Waters of Death
readings.text:
[Exodus 2:1] And a man of the house of Lĕvi went and married <dn>את</dn> a daughter of Lĕvi.
[2] And the woman conceived and bore a son. And she saw <dn>את</dn> that he was a lovely child, and she hid him three months.
[3] And when she could hide him no longer, she took an ark of wicker for him, and coated it with tar and pitch, and put <dn>את</dn> the child in it, and laid it in the reeds by the edge of the river.
[4] And his sister stood at a distance, to know what would be done to him.
[5] And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the river, and her young women were walking by the riverside. And when she saw <dn>את</dn> the ark among the reeds, she sent <dn>את</dn> her female servant to get it,
[6] and opened it and saw <dn>את</dn> the child, and see, the baby wept. So she had compassion on him, and said, “This is one of the children of the Hebrews.”
[7] And his sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Shall I go and call a nurse for you from the Hebrew women to nurse <dn>את</dn> the child for you?”
[8] And Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Go.” And the young woman went and called <dn>את</dn> the child’s mother.
[9] And Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Take <dn>את</dn> this child away and nurse him for me, then I shall pay your wages.” So the woman took <dn>את</dn> the child and nursed him.
[10] And the child grew, and she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Mosheh, saying, “Because I have drawn him out of the water.”

readings.title: The Striking of the Mitsrian
readings.subtitle: Flight to the Wilderness
readings.text:
[11] And in those days it came to be, when Mosheh was grown, that he went out to his brothers and looked at their burdens. And he saw a Mitsrian striking a Hebrew, one of his brothers.
[12] So he turned this way and that way, and when he saw no one, he struck <dn>את</dn> the Mitsrian and hid him in the sand.
[13] And he went out the second day and saw two Hebrew men fighting, and he said to the one who did the wrong, “Why do you strike your neighbour?”
[14] And he said, “Who made you a head and a judge over us? Do you intend to kill me as you killed <dn>את</dn> the Mitsrian?” And Mosheh feared and said, “Truly, the matter is known!”
[15] And Pharaoh heard of <dn>את</dn> this matter, and he sought to kill <dn>את</dn> Mosheh. But Mosheh fled from the face of Pharaoh and dwelt in the land of Miḏyan. And he sat down by a well.

readings.title: The Well of Re’u’ĕl
readings.subtitle: A Bride for the Exile
readings.text:
[16] And the priest of Miḏyan had seven daughters. And they came and drew water, and they filled <dn>את</dn> the troughs to water <dn>את</dn> their father’s flock,
[17] but the shepherds came and drove them away. Then Mosheh stood up and came to their rescue, and watered <dn>את</dn> their flock.
[18] And they came to Re’u’ĕl their father, and he said, “How is it that you have come so soon today?”
[19] And they said, “A Mitsrian rescued us from the hand of the shepherds, and he also drew enough water for us and watered <dn>את</dn> the flock.”
[20] And he said to his daughters, “And where is he? Why did you leave <dn>את</dn> the man? Call him and let him eat bread.”
[21] And Mosheh agreed to dwell with the man, and he gave <dn>את</dn> Tsipporah his daughter to Mosheh.
[22] And she bore him a son, and he called <dn>את</dn> his name Gĕreshom, for he said, “I have become a sojourner in a foreign land.”

readings.title: The Cry Ascends to Elohim
readings.subtitle: The Divine Assessment
readings.text:
[23] And it came to be after these many days that the sovereign of Mitsrayim died. And the children of Yisra’ĕl groaned because of the slavery, and they cried out. And their cry came up to <dn>Elohim</dn> because of the slavery.
[24] And <dn>Elohim</dn> heard <dn>את</dn> their groaning, and <dn>Elohim</dn> remembered <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> covenant with <dn>את</dn> Aḇraham, with <dn>את</dn> Yitsḥaq, and with <dn>את</dn> Ya‘aqoḇ.
[25] And <dn>Elohim</dn> looked on <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ĕl, and <dn>Elohim</dn> knew!

readings.subsection: The Generational Line to the Exile
readings.title: The Sons of Lĕvi and Aharon
readings.subtitle: Tracking the Spiritual Authority

readings.title: The Families of Gĕreshom, Qehath, and Merari
readings.subtitle: The Divisions of Service
readings.text:
[16] The sons of Lĕvi: Gĕreshom, Qehath, and Merari.
[17] And these are the names of the sons of Gĕreshom: Liḇni and Shim‘i.
[18] And the sons of Qehath: Amram, and Yitshar, and Ḥeḇron, and Uzzi’ĕl.
[19] The sons of Merari: Maḥli and Mushi. And these are the clans of the Lĕvites according to their fathers:
[20] Of Gĕreshom were Liḇni his son, Yaḥath his son, Zimmah his son,
[21] Yo’aḥ his son, Iddo his son, Zeraḥ his son, Ye’atherai his son.
[22] The sons of Qehath: Amminaḏaḇ his son, Qoraḥ his son, Assir his son,
[23] Elqanah his son, Eḇyasaph his son, Assir his son,
[24] Taḥath his son, Uri’ĕl his son, Uzziyah his son, and Sha’ul his son.
[25] And the sons of Elqanah: Amasai and Aḥimoth.
[26] Elqanah – the sons of Elqanah: Tsophai his son, and Naḥath his son,
[27] Eliyaḇ his son, Yeroḥam his son, Elqanah his son.
[28] And the sons of Shemu’ĕl: Yo’ĕl the first-born, and Aḇiyah the second.
[29] The sons of Merari: Maḥli, Liḇni his son, Shim‘i his son, Uzzah his son,
[30] Shim‘a his son, Ḥaggiyah his son, and Asayah his son.

readings.title: The Ministry of Prophetic Song
readings.subtitle: Appointed for the Dwelling Place
readings.text:
[31] And these are the men whom Daviḏ appointed over the service of song in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, after the ark came to rest.
[32] And they were rendering service in song before the dwelling place of the Tent of Appointment, until Shelomoh had built <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in Yerushalayim, and they performed their duties according to their ruling.
[33] And these are the ones who stood with their sons: Of the sons of the Qehathites were Hĕman the singer, son of Yo’ĕl, son of Shemu’ĕl,
[34] son of Elqanah, son of Yeroḥam, son of Eli’ĕl, son of Tovaḥ,
[35] son of Tsuph, son of Elqanah, son of Maḥath, son of Amasai,
[36] son of Elqanah, son of Yo’ĕl, son of Azaryah, son of Tsephanyah,
[37] son of Taḥath, son of Assir, son of Eḇyasaph, son of Qoraḥ,
[38] son of Yitshar, son of Qehath, son of Lĕvi, son of Yisra’ĕl.
[39] And his brother Asaph, who stood at his right hand, was Asaph son of Bereḵyahu, son of Shim‘a,
[40] son of Miḵa’ĕl, son of Ba‘asĕyah, son of Malkiyah,
[41] son of Ethni, son of Zeraḥ, son of Aḏayah,
[42] son of ĕythan, son of Zimmah, son of Shim‘i,
[43] son of Yaḥath, son of Gĕreshom, son of Lĕvi.
[44] And their brothers, the sons of Merari, on the left hand, were ĕythan son of Qishi, son of Aḇdi, son of Malluḵ,
[45] son of Ḥashaḇyah, son of Amatsyah, son of Ḥilqiyah,
[46] son of Amtsi, son of Bani, son of Shemer,
[47] son of Maḥli, son of Mushi, son of Merari, son of Lĕvi.
[48] And their brothers, the Lĕvites, were appointed to every kind of service of the Dwelling Place of the House of <dn>Elohim</dn>.

readings.title: The Atoning Service
readings.subtitle: The Line of High Priests
readings.text:
[49] But Aharon and his sons offered on the slaughter-place of ascending offering and on the slaughter-place of incense, for all the work of the Most Set-apart Place, and to make atonement for Yisra’ĕl, according to all that Mosheh the servant of <dn>Elohim</dn> had commanded.
[50] And these are the sons of Aharon: El‘azar his son, Pineḥas his son, Aḇishua his son,
[51] Buqqi his son, Uzzi his son, Zeraḥyah his son,
[52] Merayoth his son, Amaryah his son, Aḥituḇ his son,
[53] Tsaḏoq his son, Aḥima‘ats his son.

readings.title: The Cities of Refuge and Open Lands
readings.subtitle: Distributing the Lĕvites in Yisra’ĕl
readings.text:
[54] And these were their dwelling places throughout their settlements within their borders, of the sons of Aharon, of the clan of the Qehathites, for the lot was theirs.
[55] And they gave them <dn>את</dn> Ḥeḇron in the land of Yehuḏah, with its surrounding open lands.
[56] But <dn>את</dn> the fields of the city and <dn>את</dn> its villages they gave to Kalĕḇ son of Yephunneh.
[57] And to the sons of Aharon they gave <dn>את</dn> the cities of refuge: <dn>את</dn> Ḥeḇron, and <dn>את</dn> Liḇnah with its open lands, and <dn>את</dn> Yattir, and <dn>את</dn> Eshtemoa with its open lands,
[58] and <dn>את</dn> Ḥilĕn with its open lands, <dn>את</dn> Deḇir with its open lands,
[59] and <dn>את</dn> Ashan with its open lands, and <dn>את</dn> Bĕyth Shemesh with its open lands.
[60] And from the tribe of Binyamin: <dn>את</dn> Geḇa with its open lands, and <dn>את</dn> Alemeth with its open lands, and <dn>את</dn> Anathoth with its open lands. All their cities among their clans were thirteen.
[61] And to the rest of the clan of the tribe of the Qehathites by lot ten cities from half the tribe of Menashsheh.
[62] And to the sons of Gĕreshom, throughout their clans, thirteen cities from the tribe of Yissasḵar, and from the tribe of Ashĕr, and from the tribe of Naphtali, and from the tribe of Menashsheh in Bashan.
[63] To the sons of Merari, throughout their clans, by lot twelve cities from the tribe of Re’uḇĕn, and from the tribe of Gaḏ, and from the tribe of Zeḇulun.
[64] So the children of Yisra’ĕl gave <dn>את</dn> cities with <dn>את</dn> their open lands to the Lĕvites.
[65] And they gave by lot from the tribe of the children of Yehuḏah, and from the tribe of the children of Shim‘on, and from the tribe of the children of Binyamin <dn>את</dn> these cities which are mentioned by name.
[66] And some of the clans of the sons of Qehath had cities of their borders from the tribe of Ephrayim.
[67] And they gave them <dn>את</dn> the cities of refuge: <dn>את</dn> Sheḵem with its open lands, in the mountains of Ephrayim, and <dn>את</dn> Gezer with its open lands,
[68] and <dn>את</dn> Yoqme‘am with its open lands, and <dn>את</dn> Bĕyth Ḥoron with its open lands,
[69] and <dn>את</dn> Ayalon with its open lands, and <dn>את</dn> Gath Rimmon with its open lands.
[70] And from the half-tribe of Menashsheh: <dn>את</dn> Anĕr with its open lands, and <dn>את</dn> Bil‘am with its open lands, for the rest of the clan of the sons of Qehath.
[71] From the clan of the half-tribe of Menashsheh the sons of Gĕreshom: <dn>את</dn> Golan in Bashan with its open lands and <dn>את</dn> Ashtaroth with its open lands.
[72] And from the tribe of Yissasḵar: <dn>את</dn> Qeḏesh with its open lands, <dn>את</dn> Daḇerath with its open lands,
[73] <dn>את</dn> Ramoth with its open lands, and <dn>את</dn> Anĕm with its open lands.
[74] And from the tribe of Ashĕr: <dn>את</dn> Mashal with its open lands, and <dn>את</dn> Aḇdon with its open lands,
[75] and <dn>את</dn> Ḥuqoq with its open lands, and <dn>את</dn> Reḥoḇ with its open lands.
[76] And from the tribe of Naphtali: <dn>את</dn> Qeḏesh in Galil with its open lands, and <dn>את</dn> Ḥammon with its open lands, and <dn>את</dn> Qiryathayim with its open lands.
[77] From the tribe of Zeḇulun the rest of the children of Merari: <dn>את</dn> Rimmon with its open lands and <dn>את</dn> Taḇor with its open lands.
[78] And from beyond the Yardĕn of Yeriḥo, on the east side of the Yardĕn, from the tribe of Re’uḇĕn: <dn>את</dn> Betser in the wilderness with its open lands, and <dn>את</dn> Yahtsah with its open lands,
[79] <dn>את</dn> Qeḏĕmoth with its open lands, and <dn>את</dn> Mĕpha‘ath with its open lands.
[80] And from the tribe of Gaḏ: <dn>את</dn> Ramoth in Gil‘aḏ with its open lands, and <dn>את</dn> Maḥanayim with its open lands,
[81] and <dn>את</dn> Ḥeshbon with its open lands, and <dn>את</dn> Ya‘zĕr with its open lands.

readings.title: The Unconsumed Bush
readings.subtitle: The Convergence of Holy Ground
readings.text:
[Exodus 3:1] And Mosheh was shepherding <dn>את</dn> the flock of Yithro his father-in-law, the priest of Miḏyan. And he led <dn>את</dn> the flock to the back of the wilderness, and came to Ḥorĕḇ, the mountain of <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[2] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to him in a flame of fire from the midst of a bush. And he looked and saw the bush burning with fire, but the bush was not consumed.
[3] And Mosheh said, “Let me turn aside now, and see <dn>את</dn> this great sight, why the bush does not burn.”
[4] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saw that he turned aside to see, and <dn>Elohim</dn> called to him from the midst of the bush and said, <dq>Mosheh! Mosheh!</dq> And he said, “Here I am.”
[5] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>Do not come near here. Take your sandals off your feet, for the place on which you are standing is set-apart ground.</dq>
[6] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq><dn>I</dn> am the <dn>Elohim</dn> of your father, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Aḇraham, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yitsḥaq, and the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Ya‘aqoḇ.</dq> And Mosheh hid his face, for he was afraid to look at <dn>Elohim</dn>.

readings.title: The Deliverance Strategy
readings.subtitle: The Oath to Bring Them Out
readings.text:
[7] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq><dn>I</dn> have indeed seen <dn>את</dn> the oppression of <dn>My</dn> people who are in Mitsrayim, and have heard their cry because of their slave-drivers, for <dn>I</dn> know <dn>את</dn> their sorrows.</dq>
[8] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> have come down to deliver them from the hand of the Mitsrites, and to bring them up from that land to a good and spacious land, to a land flowing with milk and honey, to the place of the Kena‘anites and the Ḥittites and the Amorites and the Perizzites and the Ḥivvites and the Yeḇusites.</dq>
[9] <dq>And now, see, the cry of the children of Yisra’ĕl has come to <dn>Me</dn>, and <dn>I</dn> have also seen <dn>את</dn> the oppression with which the Mitsrites oppress them.</dq>
[10] <dq>And now, come, <dn>I</dn> am sending you to Pharaoh, to bring <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> people, the children of Yisra’ĕl, out of Mitsrayim.</dq>
[11] And Mosheh said to <dn>Elohim</dn>, “Who am I that I should go to Pharaoh, and that I should bring <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ĕl out of Mitsrayim?”
[12] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>Because <dn>I</dn> am with you. And this is to you the sign that <dn>I</dn> have sent you: When you have brought <dn>את</dn> the people out of Mitsrayim, you are to serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> on this mountain.</dq>

readings.title: I Am That Which I Am
readings.subtitle: The Eternal Memorial
readings.text:
[13] And Mosheh said to <dn>Elohim</dn>, “See, when I come to the children of Yisra’ĕl and say to them, ‘The <dn>Elohim</dn> of your fathers has sent me to you,’ and they say to me, ‘What is <dn>His</dn> Name?’ what shall I say to them?”
[14] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq><dn>I</dn> am that which <dn>I</dn> am.</dq> And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>Thus you shall say to the children of Yisra’ĕl, ‘<dn>I</dn> am has sent me to you.’</dq>
[15] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said further to Mosheh, <dq>Thus you are to say to the children of Yisra’ĕl, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of your fathers, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Aḇraham, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yitsḥaq, and the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Ya‘aqoḇ, has sent me to you. This is <dn>My</dn> Name forever, and this is <dn>My</dn> remembrance to all generations.’</dq>

readings.title: The Prophetic Blueprint
readings.subtitle: The Promise to Plunder the Oppressor
readings.text:
[16] <dq>Go, and you shall gather <dn>את</dn> the elders of Yisra’ĕl together, and say to them, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of your fathers, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Aḇraham, of Yitsḥaq, and of Ya‘aqoḇ, appeared to me, saying, “<dn>I</dn> have indeed visited <dn>את</dn> you and seen <dn>את</dn> what is done to you in Mitsrayim;</dq>
[17] <dq>and <dn>I</dn> say: <dn>I</dn> am bringing <dn>את</dn> you up out of the affliction of Mitsrayim to the land of the Kena‘anite and the Ḥittite and the Amorite and the Perizzite and the Ḥivvite and the Yeḇusite, to a land flowing with milk and honey.” ’</dq>
[18] <dq>And they shall listen to your voice. And you shall come, you and the elders of Yisra’ĕl, to the sovereign of Mitsrayim, and you shall say to him, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of the Hebrews has met with us. And now, please, let us go three days’ journey into the wilderness to slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>.’</dq>
[19] <dq>But <dn>I</dn> know that the sovereign of Mitsrayim is not going to let <dn>את</dn> you go, not even by a strong hand.</dq>
[20] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall stretch out <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> hand and strike <dn>את</dn> Mitsrayim with <dn>את</dn> all <dn>My</dn> wonders which <dn>I</dn> shall do in its midst. And after that he shall let <dn>את</dn> you go.</dq>
[21] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall give <dn>את</dn> this people favour in the eyes of the Mitsrites. And it shall be, that when you go, you shall not go empty-handed.</dq>
[22] <dq>But every woman shall ask from her neighbour and from the stranger in her house, objects of silver, and objects of gold, and garments. And you shall put them on your sons and on your daughters, and shall plunder <dn>את</dn> the Mitsrites.</dq>

readings.title: The Rod, the Leprosy, and the Blood
readings.subtitle: Physical Proofs of the Divine Presence
readings.text:
[Exodus 4:1] And Mosheh answered and said, “And if they do not believe me, nor listen to my voice, and say, ‘<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not appeared to you?’ ”
[2] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>What is that in your hand?</dq> And he said, “A rod.”
[3] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>Throw it on the ground.</dq> So he threw it on the ground, and it became a serpent. And Mosheh fled from it.
[4] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>Reach out your hand and seize it by the tail</dq> – so he reached out his hand and took hold of it, and it became a rod in his hand –
[5] <dq>so that they believe that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of their fathers, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Aḇraham, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yitsḥaq, and the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Ya‘aqoḇ, has appeared to you.</dq>
[6] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him again, <dq>Now put your hand in your bosom.</dq> And he put his hand in his bosom, and when he took it out, and see, his hand was leprous, like snow.
[7] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>Put your hand in your bosom again.</dq> So he put his hand in your bosom again, and drew it out of his bosom, and see, it was restored like his other flesh.
[8] <dq>And it shall be, if they do not believe you, nor listen to the voice of the first sign, they shall believe the voice of the latter sign.</dq>
[9] <dq>And it shall be, if they do not believe even these two signs, or listen to your voice, that you shall take water from the river and pour it on the dry land. And the water which you take from the river shall become blood on the dry land.</dq>

readings.title: The Reluctance of Mosheh
readings.subtitle: Aharon Ordained as the Prophet's Voice
readings.text:
[10] And Mosheh said to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, I am not a man of words, neither before nor since <dn>You</dn> have spoken to <dn>Your</dn> servant, for I am slow of speech and slow of tongue.”
[11] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>Who has made man’s mouth? Or who makes dumb, or deaf, or seeing, or blind? Is it not <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?</dq>
[12] <dq>And now, go, and <dn>I</dn> shall be with your mouth and teach you <dn>את</dn> what to say.</dq>
[13] But he said, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, please send by the hand of him whom <dn>You</dn> would send.”
[14] And the displeasure of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> burned against Mosheh, and <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>Is not Aharon the Lĕvite your brother? <dn>I</dn> know that he speaks well. And see, he is also coming out to meet you. And when he sees you, he shall be glad in his heart.</dq>
[15] <dq>And you shall speak to him and put <dn>את</dn> the words in his mouth. And <dn>I</dn> am with your mouth and with his mouth, and <dn>I</dn> shall teach <dn>את</dn> you <dn>את</dn> what to do.</dq>
[16] <dq>And he shall speak for you to the people. And it shall be that he shall be a mouth for you, and you shall be an elohim for him.</dq>
[17] <dq>And take <dn>את</dn> this rod in your hand, with which you shall do <dn>את</dn> the signs.</dq>

readings.title: Yisra’ĕl as the First-born Son
readings.subtitle: The Threat of the First-born Judgment
readings.text:
[18] Then Mosheh went and returned to Yether his father-in-law, and said to him, “Please let me go and return to my brothers who are in Mitsrayim to see whether they are still alive.” And Yithro said to Mosheh, “Go in peace.”
[19] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh in Miḏyan, <dq>Go, return to Mitsrayim, for all the men are dead who sought <dn>את</dn> your life.</dq>
[20] So Mosheh took <dn>את</dn> his wife and <dn>את</dn> his sons and set them on a donkey, and he returned to the land of Mitsrayim. And Mosheh took <dn>את</dn> the rod of <dn>Elohim</dn> in his hand.
[21] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>As you go back to Mitsrayim, see that you do <dn>את</dn> all those wonders before Pharaoh which <dn>I</dn> have put in your hand. But <dn>I</dn> am going to strengthen <dn>את</dn> his heart, so that he does not let <dn>את</dn> the people go.</dq>
[22] <dq>And you shall say to Pharaoh, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “Yisra’ĕl is <dn>My</dn> son, <dn>My</dn> first-born,</dq>
[23] <dq>so <dn>I</dn> say to you, let <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> son go to serve <dn>Me</dn>. But if you refuse to let him go, see, <dn>I</dn> am killing <dn>את</dn> your son, your first-born.” ’</dq>

readings.title: The Bridegroom of Blood
readings.subtitle: Aligning with the Covenantal Seal
readings.text:
[24] And it came to be on the way, in the lodging place, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> met him and sought to kill him.
[25] And Tsipporah took a sharp stone and cut off <dn>את</dn> the foreskin of her son and threw it at his feet, and said, “You are indeed a bridegroom of blood to me!”
[26] So <dn>He</dn> let him go. Then she said, “You are a bridegroom of blood,” because of the circumcision.

readings.title: The Gathering of the Elders
readings.subtitle: The Belief of the People
readings.text:
[27] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Aharon, <dq>Go to meet Mosheh in the wilderness.</dq> And he went and met him on the mountain of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and kissed him.
[28] Mosheh then told Aharon <dn>את</dn> all the words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who had sent him, and <dn>את</dn> all the signs which <dn>He</dn> had commanded him.
[29] And Mosheh went with Aharon and gathered together <dn>את</dn> all the elders of the children of Yisra’ĕl.
[30] And Aharon spoke <dn>את</dn> all the words which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had spoken to Mosheh. Then he did <dn>את</dn> the signs before the eyes of the people.
[31] And the people believed. And they heard that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had visited <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ĕl and that <dn>He</dn> had looked on <dn>את</dn> their affliction, and they bowed their heads and did obeisance.
